PARTNER.desc: A global counterparty (Ali, Jeton, PT): remittance companies, fintechs, EMIs, neobanks or crypto exchanges. How a partner is used in a project lives in PARTNER_CONFIG. disclosure_style records whether the partner’s markup is visible.

RATE_SOURCE.desc: A market data source. Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.

INTRODUCER.desc: An external introducer who brought in a client and is owed referral commission (Understanding §4.2a). Paid either a share of NPL’s earnings or a fixed % per transaction; several introducers may share one deal.

SENDER.desc: A sending party of the project (Ayush, Naveen). Which receiver groups a sender may pay is SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW. A sender’s refunds go to a RECEIVER of kind sender_return linked to it.

Payouts within a group are ordinary settlement; across groups they are offsets; with a single group no offset can arise. Groups hold counterparty receivers only (v5.0, D13): sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less.

INV: Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency.
Ledger tables are append-only; corrections are reversing transactions.
No custody in the normal path: CL.OWN.*.HELD may only be debited by a collection on a deal with an approved REROUTE; the custody aging view is the standing control.

Disburse to less than one unit: under disburse_policy = to_zero a DISBURSEMENT pays whole units and leaves only rounding dust; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project’s exposure cap (Q5, Q8).
Priced once, per leg: a leg’s pricing fields are write-once after priced_at; a re-quote is a new leg or a new deal group.

Partner fixed at quote, per leg: partner_pair_id / partner_entity_id change only through an approved REROUTE. A collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity (v5.1, D15). Its kind must match the leg’s collection_method — wallet for crypto, bank for bank, no endpoint for cash (D19, agreed 8 Oct). A COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint; a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).

Entitlement conservation: Σ GROUP_ENTITLEMENT over a project’s groups = Σ CLIENT_BALANCE over partners, per currency, including balance-conversion re-attributions. Return and hop legs preserve this because they inherit the parent leg’s group (D13).
Destination approval precedes collection: a quote-first deal cannot leave Inquiry unless at least one account in the entitled group has an approved SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION with the chosen partner.
Approver ≠ initiator on every APPROVAL; Operations never receives derived-economics fields.
Every balance shown anywhere is a sum over postings or deals.
A collect-first deal requires an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry for its sender and group (Q1).
A return leg pays the sender_return RECEIVER linked to the parent leg’s sender, unless a Management-approved exception with a reason names another approved receiver.
The failed forward line is reversed before a return leg opens, so entitlement and balance are correct at the return conversion.
A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a balance conversion.
A recovery on a reroute cannot exceed the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE at that partner; the alternate partner’s expected conversion is computed on the net amount forwarded.
Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver (Q13).

Offsets arise only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to a different group, and carry Management approval and tighter aging. A project with one group never has an offset; within a group nothing is tracked beyond an informational tally (v5.0).

A RECEIVER has a group_id if and only if kind = counterparty. Forward legs and the sender allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only. A return leg inherits receiver_group_id from its parent leg; leg n of a route inherits it from leg n−1 (v5.0, D13).

WALKS.name: Quote-first deal, end to end
steps: PROJECT
The client. Its policies (quote freshness and validity, grace, fee treatment, disburse policy and exposure cap) govern everything below.
SENDER
Operator picks the sender. The receiver groups this sender may pay are listed in SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW.
RECEIVER_GROUP
The entitled group. One of its receivers’ accounts must hold an approved registration with the chosen partner before the deal leaves Inquiry.
PARTNER_PAIR
Choosing partner × currency pair is part of pricing. Partner and facilitating entity are fixed per leg.
FEE_STRUCTURE
The versioned client-side fee for that partner × pair is stamped on the deal group.
RATE_COMPARISON
Created lazily for partner × pair × date by the first deal of the day.
MARKET_RATE
The market snapshot from the pair’s prioritised rate source.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The partner’s rate version for the day; the breach check may freeze the pair until Finance decides.
DEAL_GROUP
The client-facing instruction: pair as the sender sees it, sender rate, fee, reference. Every deal belongs to one; this one has a single leg.
DEAL
Leg 1, forward, funded by a collection. Priced once; sent / valid / grace timestamps and quote_hash recorded.
SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION
Destination approval precedes collection: an approved account of the entitled group with this partner.
COLLECTION
Funds arrive in 1..n parts into a COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT of the leg’s partner entity (bank or wallet by kind); cash with instructions on the deal.
CONVERSION

The partner converts against the exact rate version. actual_out is booked in whole units; the dropped fraction stays as client dust; the receiver fee is taken here; NPL’s margin is captured now and never again at risk.
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
One balanced transaction; margin recognition is the only client → company ownership flip.
DISBURSEMENT
Pays whole units from the partner’s holding through a SETTLEMENT_RAIL with a SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY narrative.
DISBURSEMENT_LINE
One or many destination accounts. Paying a receiver in another group creates the offset in the same action.
CONFIRMATION
The receiver confirms the amount received: full or short.
SHORTFALL
If short, a shortfall opens against the receiver and is topped up by a later disbursement.
BANK_FEE_EVENT
Post-confirmation true-up of expected vs actual bank fee: waived, carried forward or absorbed.

WALKS.name: Collect-first deal
steps: COLLECTION
Funds arrive before any quote. Attribution needs an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry (Q1); the sender is picked from the configured list.
DEAL_GROUP
Created with entry_mode collect_first; the sender is promised nothing.
DEAL
The single leg is born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; no quote clocks.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The rate version is taken at conversion rather than stamped at quote.
CONVERSION
Converted against that version; actual_out booked; margin captured.
DISBURSEMENT
Then the same whole-unit settlement as any other deal.

WALKS.name: Rejected payout and return leg
steps: DISBURSEMENT
USDT was converted to GBP at PT and paid out to the receiver’s account.
DISBURSEMENT_RETURN

The receiving or intermediary bank rejects the transfer. The GBP returns to PT minus bank fees; the line’s outcome becomes returned and a reversing transaction puts the money back into the client’s balance.
BANK_FEE_EVENT
The bounce fee is booked as expected vs actual, waived (client) or absorbed (NPL) per the project’s treatment.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
With the line reversed, the group’s entitlement is restored. Option B stops here: the GBP stays in balance for later payouts to receivers in the same group; another group would be an approved offset.
DEAL

Option A: a return leg on the same deal group. leg_type return, funding_source returned_disbursement, GBP → USDT at PT, priced at conversion. NPL’s original margin is untouched; the FX loss falls on the client’s funds.
FEE_DECISION
Markup on the return leg is applied or waived case by case, with an approver.
CONVERSION
The reverse conversion, owned by the return leg, using PT’s rate version for GBP → USDT.
RECEIVER
The destination is the sender_return receiver linked to the parent leg’s sender. Any other receiver needs Management approval, a reason, and prior registration.
RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT
The sender’s USDT wallet is one of that receiver’s accounts; it is chosen at payout and need not be the wallet the sender paid from.
DISBURSEMENT_LINE
The USDT goes out as an ordinary payout line to that account, clearing the entitlement its return leg credited to the parent leg’s group (v5.0, D13).

WALKS.name: Two-leg route via a deal group
steps: DEAL_GROUP
The sender wants INR → EUR. Ali can collect INR but cannot reach EUR, so the group will have two legs. The group holds the one price the sender saw.
DEAL
Leg 1: INR → USDT at Ali, forward, funded by the collection. Partner fixed per leg.
CONVERSION
Ali converts to USDT; margin on leg 1 is captured here.
RECEIVER
Jeton’s collection wallet is registered as a RECEIVER of kind partner_transit, so the hop is an ordinary payout.
DISBURSEMENT
Ali pays the USDT to the transit receiver’s account. Entitlement passes through the transit group.
PARTNER_CONFIG
Leg 2 is a second DEAL on the same group at Jeton: USDT → EUR, funding_source prior_leg, no collection.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
Jeton’s rate version for USDT → EUR prices leg 2 at conversion.
DISBURSEMENT_LINE
Jeton pays the EUR to the real receiver’s account. Margin across the route = group quote − both partner conversions.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
The entitled group’s tally reconciles once leg 2 converts and pays out.

WALKS.name: Ad-hoc balance conversion
steps: CLIENT_BALANCE
The client holds 5K SGD and 10K USDT at PT and must pay 15K USDT.
BALANCE_CONVERSION
Finance converts SGD → USDT at PT. Not a deal: no sender, receiver or collection. It names the group it serves (chosen split).
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
The same rate procedure applies: partner rate version, market snapshot, breach check.
FEE_DECISION
Markup is optional, decided case by case with an approver.
CONVERSION
Owned by the balance conversion; actual_out in whole units, the fraction kept as dust.
ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION
The served group’s SGD entitlement becomes USDT entitlement. Any excess over its SGD entitlement is another group’s flow, booked as an approved offset.
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
Source BalanceConversion: debit client due USDT, credit client due SGD; an earnings posting only if markup was applied.
DISBURSEMENT
The 15K USDT goes out as an ordinary disbursement.

WALKS.name: Reroute, custody and recover dues
steps: DEAL
A priced leg hits a partner problem: unavailable, limit reached, holiday, compliance hold.
REROUTE
The only way partner_pair / facilitating_entity change after quote. Pre- or post-collection; post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender (Q3). Approved by Finance.
OWN_WALLET
Contingency custody. CL.OWN.*.HELD may only be debited by a collection on a deal with an approved reroute; custody_max_hours bounds it.
PARTNER_CONFIG
The alternate partner must have applicable_for_reroute set. NPL’s cut is captured at whichever partner converts, so nothing is withheld.
EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE

With forward_and_recover_dues, NPL forwards less than the full amount and reduces its receivable at that partner by the same figure: own wallet cash up, receivable down, no income. The partner’s agreement is recorded.
CUSTODY
The custody aging view (collections under open reroutes plus recovered dues resting in the wallet, minus forwarded) is the standing control.

WALKS.name: Rate day and breach approval
steps: RATE_SOURCE
Kraken, CMC, OANDA or XE, each with a staleness threshold.
PAIR_RATE_SOURCE
The prioritised source chain for each currency pair.
MARKET_RATE
Captured rate per source and pair; cross-source slippage is a query over these.
RATE_COMPARISON
One per partner × pair × date, with 2w and 4w average spreads built from confirmed versions only. A partner may give a new rate later the same day.
PARTNER_RATE_VERSION
Breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel). Quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze; Finance may also ask for a better rate.
APPROVAL
Finance approves with a reason or rejects. Approver ≠ initiator.
USER
Roles: ops, finance, management. Operations never sees derived-economics fields.

WALKS.name: Ledger and balances
steps: CONVERSION
A source event (collection, conversion, balance conversion, disbursement, return, confirmation, bank fee event, reroute, referral, rebate, adjustment).
LEDGER_TRANSACTION
One transaction per event, append-only; a correction is a reversing transaction.
LEDGER_POSTING
Debit and credit lines that sum to zero per currency, tagged client or company and by cost component.
LEDGER_ACCOUNT
Accounts coded OWN.HOLDER.CCY.PURPOSE; client due balances are one account per project × partner × currency. ADVANCE no longer exists.
CLIENT_BALANCE
Conversions in, balance conversions across currencies, returns back in, disbursements out. Never stored; carries dust below one unit.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT
Per group and currency: forward legs’ client_net ± re-attributions − paid + returned. Σ groups = Σ client balance (invariant 7).
OFFSET
Positive = owed, negative = holding another group’s flow. Zero by construction in a single-group project.

DOC_META: NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline. Deliverable 1 — Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model, Draft v3.0. New XP Technologies Limited, 2 October 2026, Confidential. Rebuilt from "NPLify — Project Understanding v1.0" (2 Oct 2026); supersedes v2.1 in full. Draft v3.0 is for internal review before the NPL walkthrough; dependent documents (ledger design, calculation spec, state machines, roles matrix, configuration schema, cutover) are to be rebuilt against this version.
CONVENTIONS: All monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals.
Audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4: APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG, RECORD_LOCK) and apply to all master data.
Derived figures (client balance, entitlement, offsets, custody) are views over postings and deals — never stored.
Five diagrams across four domains, one schema: 1 Configuration, 2 Rates, 3 Deal/collection/conversion/reroute, 4 Disbursement/confirmation/fees/shortfalls, 5 Ledger & controls.

Configuration: A Project (= client) owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, registrations and rebate terms all hang off it.

Receivers belong to receiver groups only when kind = counterparty: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver is in exactly one group. sender_return (stands for a sender, for refunds via the ordinary payout path) and partner_transit (stands for a partner's collection endpoint, for the hop of a two-leg route) are group-less; they never appear on forward deals or allow lists, and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays it (v5.0, D13). Entitlement is tracked per group; only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
A receiving entity has one or more accounts, each with a currency and a rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION and DISBURSEMENT_LINE point at the account.

Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner’s markup is visible; PARTNER_PAIR.partner_markup_pct is known only for market_plus partners — otherwise partner cost is inferred through the rate comparison.

Collection endpoints live in one table (v5.1, D15): COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT under the partner entity, kind bank / wallet; cash-in has no record (instructions captured on the deal). Cash collections round to the nearest 100 / 500 / 1000 units by currency.

Destination approval is per partner: SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION is an account of the project’s receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying that partner’s approval status and payout details.

SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it — neither holds money, neither is a ledger holder. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance — where the sender’s funds originated; reference only, never a payout destination.

OWN_WALLET exists for rerouting and pass-through (AQN-LT-Sub is an own wallet at Aquanow); PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. INTRODUCER and REFERRAL_RULE record referral commissions NPL pays; PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records rebates a partner pays NPL.
Rates: The rate comparison for the day is the object the operator flow creates “if not done already”: one per partner × pair × date, reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.

A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate (a better rate still outside the threshold needs approval). Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.
Deal lifecycle: Every deal belongs to a DEAL_GROUP, the client-facing instruction (pair as the sender sees it, sender rate, fee, reference, entry mode). A plain deal is a group of one leg; a two-partner route has two forward legs (leg 2 funded by leg 1); a rejected payout is unwound by a return leg funded by the DISBURSEMENT_RETURN.

Entry modes: quote_first (sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late_decision), collect_first (born Collected with priced_at = conversion time) and estimate_first (indicative figure, priced at conversion).
Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg; only a REROUTE changes partner_pair_id or partner_entity_id.

Convert sub-modes: in partner_calculates, actual_out is what the partner did and is booked; expected_out is the engine’s figure; variance is the difference, an exception if beyond tolerance. The client net never changes. A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION.

The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion (Q6). Amounts are truncated to whole units at conversion; the dropped fraction stays client money in the balance and is paid when it reaches a whole unit (Q8). NPL’s margin is captured at conversion and is never at risk from a return or a forward.

One settlement model: DISBURSEMENT drains one partner’s holding into one or many DISBURSEMENT_LINEs, in whole units; under disburse_policy hold_allowed the balance may rest within the exposure cap. A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's is the offset, created by the same action; a line to a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group and is never an offset (v5.0). “Instant” is accumulate-one-then-disburse-now.

BANK_FEE_EVENT is the post-confirmation true-up with expected vs actual, and books the bounce fee on a returned line. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved apply / waive / override of markup, network or bank fee on a single deal leg, disbursement or balance conversion.

REROUTE forwards the full client amount or forwards and recovers dues (netting what the alternate partner owes NPL, within the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE, with the partner’s agreement recorded). Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.
Ledger & controls: Client money is kept as assets that say where it is — CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.COLLECTED, DUE, INTRANSIT, CL.OWN.<CCY>.HELD, CL.<RECEIVER>.<CCY>.SHORTFALL — and liabilities that say to whom NPL must deliver it: CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE (what NPL owes the client’s receivers, one account per currency) and CL.<SENDER>.<CCY>.CREDIT. Client assets equal client liabilities per currency; group entitlement is a view on the payable, not an account.

Company accounts: CO.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.POOL (NPL’s earnings resting at a partner), CO.OWN.<CCY>.WALLET (NPL’s own money in its wallet, e.g. recovered dues), REBATE_RECEIVABLE, REFERRAL_PAYABLE, and the income and expense accounts EARN_GROSS, EXP_PARTNER, EXP_BANKFEE, EXP_NETWORK, VARIANCE.
holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity: neither holds money. Project is a holder only for the PAYABLE.

Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver and nothing is withheld at source on a reroute; company → client postings exist only where NPL absorbs a fee or tops up a shortfall.

Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency; a conversion has an in-currency leg and an out-currency leg that each balance on their own. Corrections are reversing transactions that name what they reverse.

UNDERSTANDING:
NPLify — Project Understanding
Everything we currently understand about NPL’s remittance operations and the platform to be built · v1.0
New XP Technologies Limited
2 October 2026 · Working document · Confidential
How to read this. This is the consolidated understanding at the end of the first understanding block. It supersedes earlier drafts wherever they disagree (the ERD v2.1 and the P0 pack D2–D8 will be rebuilt from this document). §12 lists what changed along the way and why, so nothing that was corrected can quietly resurface. §11 lists what is still open. Nothing here is built; this is the thing we build from.
1 · What NPL does
NPL is a remittance coordinator. On behalf of its clients it arranges for money to be collected from payers, converted between currencies and rails (fiat and crypto — USDT most often), and settled to the right recipients. It does this through partners (Ali, Jeton, etc.) who do the actual conversion and hold or move the funds; NPL designs the deal, picks the partner, instructs, verifies and reconciles.
In terms of the partners, these are either remittance companies, Fintech, EMIs, Neobanks, Crypto Exchange (or a combination of these). For e.g. Ali has a few licensed remittance companies (referred to as PT – e.g. PT Global, PT Sukses, etc.). Jeton is a fintech which has a couple of different EMIs/Neobank offerings. When NPL uses a partner for a specific project, most often the facilitating entity/channel(s) are defined clearly (For e.g. Evo project via Ali will use PT Sukses).
Sometimes establishing the channel may require additional agreements between the partner/channel and the client (out of scope for NPL operations, managed at the NPL leadership level). In general, the client relationships are ring-fenced from the partners & vice-versa, so for the business to continue, NPL’s involvement is always required (meaning the partner doesn’t have any interaction with the client – all communication flows through NPL).
NPL’s income is the margin engineered into the price it quotes. Everything else in the platform — rates, fees, ledgers, offsets, approvals — exists to compute that margin, protect it, and prove it.
Today the whole operation runs on spreadsheets, messaging channels and people’s memories. The platform replaces that with a configuration-driven engine that reproduces today’s calculations exactly first, then takes over.
2 · Principles that bind everything
No custody in the normal path. Client money flows sender → partner → recipient. NPL’s own wallet is used only under a recorded, approved reroute when the intended partner cannot handle the volume (§7.1).
Priced once. A deal’s rate and fees are stamped at one moment and never recomputed (there are exceptions such as the customer makes a transfer after the rate duration expired, customer asked for a better rate, etc. – finance/management approval needed). In quote-first deals that moment is the quote; in collect-first deals it is the conversion.
Immutable, double-entry ledger. Every movement is a balanced pair of postings; nothing is edited or deleted; corrections are reversing entries; every balance is a sum, never a stored field.
Whose money is always known. Every amount carries an owner tag: client funds or company earnings. The partner’s share is a cost line, not a pot NPL holds.
Disburse to zero. A client balance exists only because the next disbursement has not happened yet. NPL never sits on client funds by choice; deliberate partial disbursement or reserves are not normal behavior. For some clients with a higher balance threshold in which case the balances sit with the partner until settled.
Nobody approves their own work; Operations never sees margins. Three cumulative roles, maker-checker on every controlled action, derived economics visible only to Finance and Management.
The FRS flow is one configuration. The Client 1 USDT→EUR flow described in the FRS must be expressible as data in this model, and must reproduce Appendix A’s figures.
3 · Configuration model
A Project is the top-level container — from the system’s point of view the project is the client (the client name is a label). A project’s Configuration has four kinds of content.
3.1 System settings (thresholds)
Max amount; system validations; frequency (daily settlement slots); rate-variation tolerances between market and agent (partner); custom conditions as the project-specific catch-all. All versioned, Finance proposes, Management approves.
3.2 Currency pairs
The project’s master list of what it trades, each with a quoting direction (units of OUT per IN, or IN per OUT), precision (5 dp standard; 8 dp for sub-unit pairs such as USDT→BTC), and the reference-rate source chain for that pair.
Note – for cash collections, the cash currency is always rounded off to the nearest 100, 500 or 1000 units (depending on the currency value). For e.g. INR is rounded to nearest 1000, SGD, USD is rounded to nearest 100
3.3 Receivers and senders (project level, partner-independent)
A Receiver is a counterparty on the receiving side and is the group: a party with one or more receiving entities (Sud → NewXP Entity, ReferScout Entity; Raj → VoiceAIWrapper). Receiving entities carry name and bank details.
A Sender is a single paying party (Ayush, Naveen) with a sendable_to allow-list naming which receiver(s) their money may go to (Ayush → Raj only; Naveen → Sud only). One receiver is the common case; the model allows a list.
There is an exception where the funds could be “temporarily” sent to another receiver (within the same project/client) and then reclaimed when new collections for the other receiver/group are done – referenced in 6.3
Senders and receivers are not tied to a partner: the same Ayush → Raj flow may run through Ali today and Jeton tomorrow.
3.4 Partner configuration (one block per partner, within the project)
How a given partner is used in this project:
---
Element | Meaning
Currency pair(s) | Which of the project’s pairs this partner handles
Fees | NPL’s client-side fee for this partner × pair (see §4)
Facilitating entities/Channel | The partner’s legal vehicles (Ali → PT-tour, PT Global Inc, …); name, optional bank details
Collection - Wallet configuration | Crypto-in endpoints (wallets per facilitating entity / network)
Collection — receiving entities | Bank-in endpoints on the partner side (name, bank details)
Collection — sending entities | Provenance reference: the actual account the sender’s funds originate from (their own bank account or one of their clients’). Reference only — says where the money came from, does not change the sender or the destination
Settlement — receiving entities | The project’s receiving entities registered with this partner (NewXP under Ali, NewXP under Jeton …) carrying that partner’s approval status and the bank details it pays to. Destination approval is therefore per partner
Settlement — sending entities | Narrative reference: the name the transfer goes out under — what the receiver sees on their statement
Settlement — facilitating entities | The rail: the bank or EMI used to execute the transfer. Not a hop; the money never rests there
---
Collection endpoints are three kinds by method: crypto-in → wallet, bank-in → collection receiving entity, cash-in → nothing pre-configured (instructions are issued at transaction time).
4 · Pricing model
4.1 How partners disclose their price
A partner either (a) gives NPL a rate with its markup already inside it, or (b) states market + x%. In case (b) the partner’s cost is explicit; in case (a) it is invisible and must be inferred by comparing the partner’s rate with market references.
4.2 How NPL prices the client
NPL’s markup sits on either the partner rate + x% or market + x%, where NPL’s x% is larger than the partner’s so the margin survives. The fee is set per partner × currency pair — the same USDT→EUR flow is priced differently to the client depending on whether Ali or Jeton handles it. Choosing the partner is therefore part of pricing.
Fee parameters per partner × pair: basis (market | partner), total percentage, split between sender and receiver (sender’s share is embedded in the sender rate; receiver’s share is deducted from the client-net), mode fixed | variable, and per-sender overrides (may be zero).
Variable mode sets the fee to protect a margin floor against the partner’s current spread, within a floor and a cap; a quote that cannot reach the floor proceeds only with Finance approval (“below-margin”).
The one unknown in the model: when NPL prices on market + x% but the partner priced style (a), NPL’s realised margin = NPL’s x% minus the partner’s hidden markup. The variance history exists for this, and the minimum-margin check must be live at conversion, not only assumed at quote.
4.2a NPL paying Referral Commissions:
Sometimes NPL has to pay referral commissions to external introducers who brought in the client. This can involve a) sharing the NPL’s earnings in a predetermined ratio OR b) a fixed % for each party involved. There could also be multiple people involved in the same deal. E.g.
Scenario 1 - John brought a new client and expects to get 1% fixed on each transaction. NPL can keep its fee fixed or variable but has to apply john’s 1% into the sender-facing rate.  So, if the fee structure is of partner rate + markup, then markup will include NPL’s fee + john’s 1%
Scenario 2 – John and James are 2 parties that want a share of the earnings. NPL decides to markup 0.5% for itself, 0.25% for john and 0.25% for james.
4.2b NPL getting commissions:
In some cases (e.g. Evo project via Jeton), they give back a % of the fee they charge on the transaction. So if Jeton charges 1.25%, they give back 0.4% back from that fee. This needs to be tracked and reconciled (summary of all transactions, fees generated, expected commissions) every month. After the reconciliation, Jeton would pay this commission back to NPL (via crypto usually).
4.3 Rates, comparison and variance
Reference rate per pair from a source chain (Kraken → CoinMarketCap for crypto pairs; Oanda/XE as adapters for fiat), snapshotted at the pricing moment with source and time. Multiple sources per pair make cross-source slippage (XE vs Oanda vs Kraken) a tracked quantity, not a surprise.
A rate comparison for the day (partner × pair) is created lazily by the first deal that needs it and reused by every deal that day. It records the partner’s rate version, the market snapshot, the spread, and the rolling 2-week / 4-week average of confirmed spreads. Occasionally the partner may give a new rate for the day, so same pair may have different versions on the same day.
A partner rate whose spread exceeds the rolling average by more than the configured relative tolerance is breached: quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a recorded reason or rejects (or asks for a better rate). Better rate doesn’t guarantee that the new rate will be under the threshold, and if it’s outside the threshold, then finance/management approval is needed. No skip path.
Partner rate versions are never overwritten; a conversion always references the exact version it used.
5 · The deal
5.1 Two entry modes
---
| Quote → Collect → Convert | Collect → Convert
What happens | Sender wants a target outcome (1,000 USD); the quote works backwards (≈ 1,004 USDT at 0.4 %); sender pays the quoted amount | Sender simply sends (1,000 USDT); NPL converts at the then-current rate and fee (996 USD)
Pricing moment | Quote | Conversion
What’s promised | Exact in and exact out | Nothing — amount out follows the rate at conversion
Who bears rate movement | NPL (hence validity, grace and drift clocks) | The sender
Lifecycle entry | Inquiry → Quoted → Accepted → Collecting | Born at Collected
Mode | Target-out (or fixed-in) | Always fixed-in
Direction of conversion pair | Sender would ask for specific value conversion. So if the pair is USDT-EUR, the conversion direction will be EUR>>USDT (i.e. “conversion needed currency” >> “collection currency”) | Conversion direction is always “collection currency” >> “conversion currency”
---
There is another scenario where instead of a fixed “upfront quote”, NPL gives an estimate. And then the conversion is done after the collection is completed.
5.2 Building the deal (operator flow)
Sender selected → the receiver from sendable_to is shown (display only; the entity within it is chosen at settlement).
Currency pair selected → partners configured for that pair → partner chosen → fee structure for partner × pair applies automatically → mode chosen (quote-first / collect-first) → the rate the fee basis needs is entered (partner rate or market rate) → the day’s rate comparison is created if it does not exist.
Facilitating entity of the chosen partner selected → its wallet / bank details / cash instructions become the “address” in the message.
Draft message for the customer: calculation (quote-first), address, references. Partner and facilitating entity are therefore fixed at quote time; only a reroute changes them.
Collection: hash / slip / receipt verified → status changes. Parts are allowed (80K today, 20K tomorrow). Overpayment → sender credit; underpayment → wait, or void with disposition.
Convert, in one of two sub-modes: NPL calculates and instructs the partner, or the partner calculates and NPL verifies. In the second, the partner’s actual figure is what is booked; the engine’s expectation is the comparison; the difference is variance, and an exception opens if beyond tolerance. The deal does not wait — the money already moved.
Settlement (§6).
5.3 Quote clocks and the late decision
Freshness (package must be marked sent within minutes of the snapshot) → validity (per client, e.g. 60 min) → grace (e.g. 15 min, only if market drift ≤ 0.10 %) → late decision: either re-quote at today’s rate with a fresh deal reference, or — if the project’s policy allows — honour the old rate as a relationship call with recorded Finance approval. The original quote stamp never changes; only the decision to accept against it does.
5.4 Destination approval
For destinations that need the partner’s approval, approval happens before collection: the route is approved, NPL confirms money can reach the destination, and only then collects. Never hold what you cannot deliver.
6 · Settlement, balances and offsets
6.1 The client balance is per partner
After conversion, funds sit with the partner that converted them. The ledger keeps one due balance per (client × partner × currency); the client-level balance is the sum across partners and is never stored
6.2 One settlement model
Accumulate (a balance exists) → disburse (the balance goes to zero; one disbursement may split across one or several destinations) → receiver confirms → fee adjustments per project. “Instant” settlement is simply accumulate-one-deal-then-disburse-now; there is one path with a timing policy, not two modes.
A disbursement draws from one partner’s holding and goes out through that partner’s settlement sending entity (narrative) via its facilitating entity (rail) to receiving entities registered with that partner. Emptying the client balance may take one disbursement per partner that holds something; a residual at Jeton while Ali is at zero is still a non-zero balance.
6.3 Entitlement and offsets
sendable_to says whose flow a collection belongs to; the converted money nonetheless lands in the shared client balance. So receiver entitlement is a tracking layer on the balance: “of this balance, Sud’s flow accounts for X, Raj’s for Y.”
Offsets are arithmetic on that layer, not movements of money:
Tier 1 — within a receiver: Sud’s money cannot reach NewXP, so it is paid to ReferScout (also Sud’s). Entitlement unchanged; the tally records which of Sud’s entities holds which share.
Tier 2 — across receivers: only when every entity of a receiver is blocked is its flow paid to another receiver (Sud → Raj). The tally shows a receiver holding more than its entitlement.
Both are the same number — entitlement − paid per receiver — and clear as later disbursements favour whoever is behind. Tier 2 is the heavier event (money with a party it does not belong to) and carries higher approval and tighter aging.
A disbursement that crosses receivers creates the tier-2 figure in the same action; nobody has to remember to record it.
6.4 Fee adjustments at settlement
Receiver-side fee (the 0.60 %-style share): computed before disbursement because it determines the amount sent. This should be computed at the time of conversion and balance attribution. Otherwise, the balance will be incorrect, if the receiver side fee is only deducted at the time of settlement.
Bank / payout fees: a true-up after confirmation, per the project’s treatment:
---
Treatment | Example (we send €8,500; bank takes €50)
Waived | Client receives €8,450 and does not ask for it back — fee on the client; memo only
Carry-forward | Client receives €8,450 and asks for it next time — NPL owes €50, added to the next disbursement
Absorbed (gross-up) | NPL expects the €50 and sends €8,550 so the client nets €8,500 — NPL’s cost. Expected vs actual difference is tracked, never lost
---
Default per client, overridable per settlement with approval.
7 · Exceptions
7.1 Rerouting (the only time NPL holds funds)
When the partner intended to handle the volume is unavailable (outage, limit reached, holiday, compliance hold), a deal is moved onto a pre-approved contingency route: collection into NPL’s own wallet, onward to an alternate partner from the project’s applicable set. Rerouting is a controlled action (Ops requests, Finance approves, reason recorded).
On a rerouted deal NPL chooses what to forward: the full amount (partner converts everything; earnings settle back later), withhold its own earnings at source, or withhold and recover dues — earnings from earlier direct deals still parked at that partner, recovered by short-paying the partner now. Eligibility for withholding depends on route, partner, sender risk and other criteria Finance will define. Recovery is an asset moving from the partner’s wallet to NPL’s, never new income, and every deduction names the deal it recovers.
When the alternate partner is chosen at conversion time and NPL’s fee rides on the partner rate, the quote was priced on a quoting-basis rate (default: the worst applicable partner rate) and the gap to the actual partner rate posts as basis variance on earnings, with the margin floor re-checked.
Custody position for NPL sign-off: NPL’s wallet holds client funds only under a recorded reroute; every resting balance has a deal, a reason and an age; outbound transfers from NPL’s wallet are dual-approved (Finance + Management) and executed by NPL signers outside the platform (hardware or multisig). The regulatory posture of contingency holding is for NPL’s counsel.
7.1.1 Pass-through / Double Conversions:
There are occasions where the route is not a direct one – meaning the partner can collect a currency but can’t convert to the expected currency. In such cases, NPL requests the collection to be done in an interim currency pair and then sends the resulting/converted currency to a different route/partner. E.g. the client wants NPL to collect INR and settle in AED. Ali can collect INR>USDT, but not AED, so the converted USDT is sent to Jeton who is able to send USDT>AED - (this is not a real example just an illustration). While this can be handled as 2 different transactions, it would be good to see if we can group it into a single transaction.
Another scenario is that the sender wants NPL to collect INR and pay EUR to vendors (receivers). However, Ali doesn’t have an available banking channel for these transfers. The vendor/receiver can however receive USDT. NPL can either a) ask Ali to settle the USDT direct to the client OR b) ask Ali to pay into NPL’s wallet and NPL then sends the outgoing transfer from its own wallet. This scenario is real and applicable in cases where NPL is reselling certain gaming solutions (in essence NPL is acting as its own remittance client). – probably out of scope from remittance platform standpoint/to be reviewed.
7.2 Other exception paths
---
Situation | Handling
Quote expires | §5.3 late decision
Deal voided before money | State change with reason; no ledger postings
Deal voided after collection | Refund (network-fee policy to decide), or funds kept as sender credit, or hold — Management approves the disposition
Partner rate breach | §4.3 — freeze until Finance approves or rejects
Reference feed outage | Fallback source; both down → manual rate with Finance approval and evidence
Destination blocked (holiday, in-transit) | §6.3 offsets — same receiver’s other entities first, another receiver only if all are blocked
Partner holiday | Partner-specific calendars: e.g. no rate but collections open, or conversions open but settlements paused
Erroneous posting | Reversing transaction plus correct transaction; nothing edited
---
8 · Money ownership and the ledger
Client funds: everything from collection to confirmed delivery. NPL coordinates, never owns.
Company earnings: the only money in NPL’s own accounts. Recognised at conversion: the sender’s stamped price fixes the client-net; whatever remains after converting exactly the client-net is NPL’s gross margin, which physically rests at the partner as a pool (the FRS’s “PT Comms” residual). That pool is NPL’s earnings receivable at that partner.
Partner cost: deducted from the pool on the partner’s fee cycle. Total cost to the client = partner cost + NPL’s earnings, and both are sums over postings carrying a cost component (earnings, partner_cost, bank_fee, network_fee, variance). The partner cost is deducted at transaction level (there is no cost accumulation or total cost paid later, etc.
Ownership flips from client to company at exactly three events: margin recognition at conversion; withholding at source on a rerouted deal; an advance to a receiver (company money paid ahead, repaid as entitlement accrues).
Shortfalls (confirmed-short deliveries) are tracked and topped up on the next settlement, funded from the pool.
Standing identities checked daily: client due per partner = Σ receiver entitlements; pool per partner = partner-stated comms balance ± logged difference; exposure (due + in-transit) ≤ policy; own-wallet holdings = 0 unless an open reroute; offsets = Σ (entitlement − paid); each confirmation = its in-transit amount exactly.
9 · Roles and controls
Operations quotes, verifies, prepares, instructs. Sees operational fields, sender-facing prices and partner rates as entered. Never sees reference rate at capture, spread, margin, comms, cost breakdown, ledgers or earnings — on any screen, export, message or report.
Finance sees all of that, approves what Ops initiates (quotes, rates, conversions, settlements, exceptions), owns reconciliation and the Finance Log.
Management sees everything, approves escalations: settlements above limit, third same-day slot, advances, offset redirections, shortfall top-ups, contingency routes, own-wallet outbound (mandatory), configuration changes, user changes, post-money voids. Countersigns releases when only one Finance user is on shift.
Visibility is cumulative (Ops ⊂ Finance ⊂ Management); gating is server-side; approver ≠ initiator is enforced at the endpoint; every controlled action is audited with actor, time, reason and record version.
Identity: Google Workspace SSO only.
10 · Reporting and reconciliation
Finance Log is the reporting spine: every posting, every approval, time-travel to any past moment because nothing was edited.
Daily reconciliation: platform vs partner statements vs bank slips; breaks become logged exceptions; small persistent gaps (rounding, partner charges) accumulate as shortfalls topped up monthly.
Calculation-comparison reports during test runs: system-computed figures beside the spreadsheet’s, per deal and per identity.
Custody aging report: every balance in NPL’s wallet by deal, reason and hours since collection.
Partner Commissions report for reconciliation (referenced in 4.2b)

DECISIONS:
ERD REVIEW DECISION RECORD (6–7 October 2026). Full record: "NPLify ERD Review — Decision Record" (Claude Doc). Summary:
SCENARIOS REVIEWED AGAINST v3.0. (1) Rejected payout: USDT → GBP at PT, bank rejects, GBP returns minus fees. Option A convert back to USDT and pay the client with case-by-case markup; option B hold the GBP for later payouts to receivers of the same client. v3.0: no returned outcome, no reverse conversion, no destination for a sender, no case-by-case fee. (2) Two-leg route: INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton; deals must link. v3.0: no deal link, no partner-to-partner move, leg 2 has no sender, no single client price. (3) Ad-hoc balance conversion: 5K SGD + 10K USDT at PT → convert SGD to pay 15K USDT. v3.0: a conversion must belong to a deal; no fee decision without a sender; entitlement breaks across currencies. Root cause: v3.0 models only the single-partner deal.
DECISIONS. D1 receiver groups (design F): project → receiver group → receiver → receiving entity → account; one default group per project; entitlement per group; offsets only across groups; a single group has no offset; reason: payouts within a pot are ordinary settlement, new receiving entities weekly need no re-attribution; alternatives rejected: project flag, separate projects per pot, receiver pooling by self-reference, attribution to sender, per-deal buckets. D2 deal legs: DEAL gains deal_group_id, leg_no, leg_type forward/return, funding_source collection/returned_disbursement/prior_leg; priced once and partner fixed per leg; DEAL_GROUP holds the client-facing quote; every deal is a group of one or more legs; rejected: generic balance-operation table. D3 receiver kinds: counterparty / sender_return (stands for a sender) / partner_transit (stands for a partner endpoint); keeps one payout path and partner destination approval; refund destination account chosen at payout, not tied to provenance wallet; third-party refund only with Management approval, reason and pre-registered receiver; sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less (v5.0 D13 removed the v4.0 return group), never on forward deals or allow lists; rejected: SENDER_ACCOUNT and a widened destination. D4 balance conversion as its own action (BALANCE_CONVERSION), not a leg: no sender/receiver/collection, Finance-initiated, may serve several payouts; chosen-group split with ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION; a CONVERSION has exactly one owner. D5 FEE_DECISION: one-off apply/waive/override with approver for markup on return legs and balance conversions, network-fee override (Q7), bank-fee override. D6 DISBURSEMENT_RETURN and a returned outcome on the line; reversing posting; bounce fee via BANK_FEE_EVENT. D7 RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (Q4).
REVIEW ANSWERS. Advances: never (ADVANCE removed). Rounding: truncate to whole units at conversion; dust stays client money, carried and paid when whole; disburse to less than one unit. Withholding: dissolved, margin always captured at conversion; ownership flips at one event only. Recover dues: yes, netted against forwarded funds, recorded with partner agreement. Entitlement split on balance conversion: chosen group. Third-party refunds: exception only. FX loss on a return leg: on the client’s funds; waiving markup only means no second cut. Legs share a DEAL_GROUP.
STILL OUTSTANDING. Q9 FRS figure reconciliation; Q11 reference workbooks.
DOCUMENT UPDATES. PERFORMANCE. No throughput concern at NPL volume; weight moves to the entitlement view and write-time checks; recommendation: a running-balance row per ledger account as a verified cache so the exposure cap is a single row read; indexes on postings (account, currency), deals (group, currency, deal_group), receivers (group), accounts (entity), polymorphic refs (type, id), accruals (partner, period), posted_at.

SCENARIOS.story: The sender sends USDT; the partner (PT) converts it to GBP. PT initiates the bank transfer to the receiver, but the receiving or intermediary bank rejects it and the money comes back to PT as GBP minus bank fees. No retry is made. NPL then has two options: (1) convert the GBP back to USDT at the partner’s rate, applying an NPL markup case by case, and send it to the client; or (2) hold the GBP in the client’s balance at PT for future outgoing transfers to other receivers.
trace: Handled. A normal DEAL with a crypto-in COLLECTION to the partner’s WALLET and a CONVERSION booking actual_out in GBP. NPL’s margin is recognised at this point and the client’s GBP balance at PT (CL.PT.GBP.DUE) rises.
PT pays out, the bank rejects

Not handled cleanly. The payout is a DISBURSEMENT_LINE and the only outcomes modelled are a CONFIRMATION with result full or short. There is no “returned” / “rejected” outcome, so nothing records that the line failed and the money came back.

Ledger side works: invariant 2 allows a reversing LEDGER_TRANSACTION that moves the GBP from INTRANSIT back into the client’s DUE balance at PT. The bank’s deduction fits BANK_FEE_EVENT (expected vs actual; waived / carry_forward / absorbed decides whether the client or NPL eats it), though that entity was meant for post-confirmation true-ups.
Option 2: hold the GBP for other receivers

Mostly handled. The balance is already per project × partner × currency, so once the reversal is posted the GBP is simply balance again and the next DISBURSEMENT from PT can pay any receiver registered with PT. Paying a different receiver creates a tier-2 offset tracked by the OFFSET view, which Sud’s comments explicitly allow; letting it sit at PT is covered by Sud’s answer to open question 5 subject to the exposure threshold. One fix needed: the failed line must be voided or reversed, otherwise RECEIVER_ENTITLEMENT treats the original receiver as already paid.
Option 1: convert GBP back to USDT and send to the client

Not handled. (a) No reverse conversion: a deal’s partner × pair is fixed at quote (invariant 6) and pricing is write-once (invariant 5), so GBP→USDT cannot be a second CONVERSION on the same deal, and a new DEAL needs a COLLECTION with an endpoint and evidence — there is no way to fund a deal from an existing balance. (b) No destination: DISBURSEMENT_LINE must point at a SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION of a RECEIVING_ENTITY; the client’s or sender’s USDT wallet is not one, and SENDER carries no payout details. (c) No case-by-case markup: FEE_STRUCTURE and FEE_OVERRIDE are standing rules, so a one-off decision to add or waive markup on this transaction has no record (the same gap as open question 7). (d) NPL’s margin from the first conversion is already booked; whether it is kept, re-earned or given back, and who bears the partner’s spread on the second conversion, is specified nowhere.
SCENARIOS.verdict: Option 2 (hold the GBP in balance) is supported once a “returned” outcome exists for a disbursement line; option 1 (re-convert to USDT and send to the client) is not supported by ERD v3.0.
SCENARIOS.fix: A return record on the disbursement line (returned amount, bank fee, reason, date); a reverse-conversion deal that can be funded from the client balance and is linked to the original deal; a payout destination for the client / sender (a USDT wallet account, which fits Sud’s answer to open question 4 on accounts with currency and rail); and a per-transaction fee decision (markup added or waived) with an approver, plus a rule for who bears the FX round-trip loss.

SCENARIOS.name: Two-leg route across two partners (INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton)
SCENARIOS.story: The sender expects INR → EUR via Ali, but Ali cannot reach EUR. In practice NPL collects INR at Ali and converts to USDT (deal 1), then sends the USDT to Jeton who converts to EUR and pays the receiver (deal 2). Deal 1 must be connected to deal 2.
trace: Handled in v3.0 as a normal DEAL: INR collected at Ali, CONVERSION to USDT, client USDT balance at Ali rises.
Moving the USDT from Ali to Jeton
Not handled in v3.0. A DISBURSEMENT can only reach a receiver’s registered account and Jeton’s collection wallet is not one; a REROUTE keeps the currency pair; the ledger has no transfer source.
Not handled in v3.0. Every DEAL needs a configured SENDER and a COLLECTION; the USDT arriving at Jeton comes from Ali.
Linking the deals and pricing the client
Not handled in v3.0. No deal-to-deal link, and no partner handles INR → EUR so the sender’s single quote has no home.
SCENARIOS.fix: A client-facing deal group above the legs; a leg funded from the prior leg instead of a collection; a payout destination for the partner hop.

SCENARIOS.name: Ad-hoc conversion of a client balance (5K SGD → USDT to pay 15K USDT)
SCENARIOS.story: A client holds 5K SGD and 10K USDT at PT and needs to pay 15K USDT to a receiving entity. NPL converts the SGD to USDT using the normal rate procedure (market and previous partner rate), with markup applied or waived case by case, then pays the 15K.
trace: Handled in v3.0: one due account per project × partner × currency (CL.PT.SGD.DUE, CL.PT.USDT.DUE).
Handled in v3.0: RATE_COMPARISON, PARTNER_RATE_VERSION and MARKET_RATE hang off PARTNER_PAIR, not the deal.
Not handled in v3.0. CONVERSION requires a DEAL, and a deal needs a sender, receiver and collection.
Not handled in v3.0. Fees are standing per partner × pair or per sender; no one-off decision exists.
Not handled in v3.0. Converting SGD balance leaves SGD entitlement standing while the SGD is gone, breaking invariant 7.
SCENARIOS.fix: A balance-conversion action separate from deals, a per-transaction fee decision, and a re-attribution of entitlement across currencies.

SCENARIO_V4.S1: Resolved. DISBURSEMENT_RETURN records the rejected line (outcome returned) and a reversing posting puts the GBP back; the bounce fee is a BANK_FEE_EVENT. Option B needs nothing more: the GBP is balance for any receiver in the same RECEIVER_GROUP (another group is an approved offset). Option A is a return leg on the same DEAL_GROUP (leg_type return, funding_source returned_disbursement, GBP → USDT priced at conversion), markup by FEE_DECISION, paid to the sender_return RECEIVER’s chosen RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT. NPL’s margin stays captured; the FX loss is on the client’s funds.
SCENARIO_V4.S2: Resolved. One DEAL_GROUP holds the INR → EUR quote with two legs. Leg 1 (INR → USDT at Ali) pays Jeton’s collection wallet, registered as a RECEIVER of kind partner_transit, through a normal DISBURSEMENT_LINE. Leg 2 (USDT → EUR at Jeton) has funding_source prior_leg and no collection. Partner is fixed per leg; margin across the route is the group quote minus both conversions.
SCENARIO_V4.S3: Resolved. BALANCE_CONVERSION (SGD → USDT at PT) is its own Finance-approved action using the same PARTNER_RATE_VERSION and MARKET_RATE machinery; markup is a FEE_DECISION; the CONVERSION it owns truncates to whole units with the fraction kept as client dust; ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION moves the served group’s SGD entitlement to USDT (chosen split, excess booked as an approved offset); then an ordinary DISBURSEMENT pays the 15K USDT.
